Starachowice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Starachowice, Poland

Not demolished. Starachowice's Jewish community, first settled in the 19th century, numbered about 3,900 in 1934, most of them murdered by the Germans in 1942. This cemetery, established in 1891, was the site of German executions during the war, with victims' bodies buried there; people murdered in Starachowice as late as the end of 1945 were likely also buried here. The cemetery survived the war in relatively good condition but was devastated in the following decades, with tombstones stolen and parts of the land built over with houses. In the 1990s, the remaining vacant portion was fenced, financed by city authorities and the Wiecznej Pamięci ('Eternal Memory') Foundation, and it is now cared for by city authorities, local activists, and Starachowice Jews living abroad. About 400 tombstones survive, along with the visible foundations of an unidentified rabbi or tzaddik's ohel.
